clue.text: Game and a drink after hard work

indicators.note: after places the drink behind the hard work in the answer

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
OP, short for opus, is a work
Scotch is whisky, a drink

explanation.surface: A player enjoys a game and then a whisky once the hard work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground pastime of hopping between chalked squares, so it is a game.

clue.text: Transmits with no difficulty

definitions.meaning: passes on to the next generation, as an heirloom
easily, as a winning racehorse ridden without urging

explanation.surface: A broadcaster sends signals effortlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is passes on to descendants; the other is an idiom for winning easily.

clue.text: Briefly stop with hands to ears

indicators.note: to ears signals that the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: paws are hands, informally

explanation.surface: Someone stops for a moment, cupping hands to ears to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: A short halt is a brief stop.

clue.text: Scots lament crown being over church

indicators.note: in a down clue being over puts the crown above the church

parts.note: a corona is a crown

explanation.surface: Scots mourn as a crown is placed above the church.
explanation.walkthrough: CORONACH is a Gaelic funeral dirge.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland funeral song or dirge, a Scottish lament.

clue.text: Screen put up to protect priest at end of nave

indicators.note: to protect means the reversed word wraps around the priest
up in a down clue means the word put is read from the bottom up

parts.note: to set is to put
Levi founded the priestly tribe, the Levites

indicators.note: at end of selects the last letter of nave

explanation.surface: A screen is put up around a priest at the far end of the nave.
explanation.walkthrough: Levi founded the tribe of Levites, Israel's hereditary priests; 'up' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to broadcast it on television.

clue.text: Girl shows great cheerfulness without it

indicators.note: without means the word it is removed from the longer word

parts.note: hilarity is great merriment

explanation.surface: A girl shows great cheer without any reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A given name, here used for a woman, so a girl.

clue.text: Finally dispatch second young boxer

parts.note: MO, a moment, is a second
a puppy is a young dog, and a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A trainer's second finishes off a young fighter in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter but here is the dog breed, whose young is a PUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear away the last remnants of something is to deal with it finally, so the phrase means finally dispatch.

clue.text: Lose minutes getting on to island

indicators.note: getting on to places the minutes next to the island

parts.note: Islay is a Scottish island in the Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone loses time boarding the ferry to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To misplace something is to lose it.

clue.text: Very close to professional team colleague

parts.note: pro is short for professional
XI, eleven, is a team in football or cricket
a mate is a colleague, workmate

explanation.surface: A professional sits right beside a teammate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearest, immediately adjacent, means very close to.

clue.text: Representative of the Church Militant?

parts.note: the Church Militant is a term for Christians on earth, but read as armed forces it suggests a forces clergyman

explanation.surface: Who stands for the Church on earth in its struggle?
explanation.definitionFit: A military chaplain is a clergyman serving with soldiers, the Church among the militant.

clue.text: Impartial person's nature corrupted by money

indicators.note: corrupted means the letters of nature are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: L, for pound (libra), is money

explanation.surface: An impartial person's good nature is spoiled by bribes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' is the anagram signal; L for pound comes from Latin libra, the source of the £ sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes no side in a dispute is called a non-aligned party, an impartial person.

clue.text: Caught girl with dictionary

parts.note: a lass is a girl
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A girl was caught out holding a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Roped with a looped rope, as a cowboy does, means caught.

clue.text: Envelope 'c' fills with a number of flyers

indicators.note: fills means the letter goes inside the envelope word

parts.note: skin is an envelope, an outer covering
the printed letter c is an OCR misreading of e, the letter that goes inside

explanation.surface: A letter c is stuffed into an envelope along with some leaflets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyers' look like leaflets but are birds: a flight of wild geese is so called.
explanation.definitionFit: The collective noun for wild geese in flight, a group of flying birds.

clue.text: Poor relatives prepared to do a variety of jobs

definitions.text: prepared to do a variety of jobs

indicators.note: poor means the letters of relatives are badly arranged into something new

explanation.surface: Impoverished relatives will take on any work going.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-round, adaptable worker is ready to turn a hand to many different tasks.

clue.text: Gloomy, but recovered from eye problem

parts.note: to be over an illness is to have recovered from it
a cast is a squint, a problem with the eye

explanation.surface: Someone is downcast despite getting over a squint.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouded skies make the weather dull and dark, which is gloomy.

clue.text: Strive to find vessel for Cook

definitions.meaning: Captain James Cook sailed this ship to the Pacific

explanation.surface: A chef tries to find a suitable pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a chef seeking a pot; it is the explorer Captain Cook and his ship.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is make a determined effort; the other is the name of Captain Cook's ship.

clue.text: Bitterly complain of train guide

definitions.meaning: a track's metal bar guides the train's wheels

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles about the railway guidebook.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to protest angrily; the other is a steel track bar that keeps trains on course.

clue.text: Revolutionary met Lenin — a mark of distinction

indicators.note: revolutionary means the letters of met Lenin a are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A revolutionary met Lenin, which was a mark of distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinctive feature, especially of the face, is a characteristic mark.

clue.text: Carefully select those chosen to bring in the banana crop?

definitions.text: those chosen to bring in the banana crop?
definitions.meaning: a bunch of bananas is a hand, and a pick is a selection, so a whimsical name for the chosen harvest

explanation.surface: Workers are picked carefully to harvest the bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: To choose each item personally is to select carefully; bananas grow in bunches called hands.

clue.text: Rings up to be disparaging

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: hoops are rings, two of them here

explanation.surface: A caller rings up only to be dismissive.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss scornfully is to be disparaging.

clue.text: Signs agreement in synod session -

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words synod session

explanation.surface: Church delegates assent during a meeting of the synod.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipping the head is a gesture showing assent, so it signs agreement.

clue.text: Emperor responsible for Boxer oppression

definitions.meaning: in Orwell's Animal Farm the pig of this name exploits Boxer, the loyal carthorse

explanation.surface: An emperor was to blame for crushing the Boxer Rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boxer Rebellion in China tempts a historical reading; Boxer is the horse in Animal Farm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the French ruler and Orwell's tyrannical pig share this name.

clue.text: I show pleasure about comparison

indicators.note: about means the smile word goes round the letter I

parts.note: to smile is to show pleasure

explanation.surface: I smile at a pleasant comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech likening one thing to another with like or as is a comparison.

clue.text: Strip and enter the water as of old

parts.note: to dive is to enter the water head first
ST is the old verb ending

explanation.surface: Swimmers undress and plunge in, as in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as of old' signals the archaic second-person ending -EST on DIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To divest is to strip, as of clothes or possessions.

clue.text: Pleased to have something finally approved

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of something

parts.note: ratified means formally approved

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to have a thing finally signed off.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling satisfied or delighted is being pleased.

clue.text: Express amazement about king's understanding

indicators.note: about means the gasp word goes round the king

parts.note: to gasp is to express amazement
R, for rex, is king

explanation.surface: A king's understanding is greeted with astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm comprehension of a subject is an understanding of it.

clue.text: Hercules, young daredevil, removed all heads belonging to this

definitions.text: Hercules, young daredevil, removed all heads belonging to this

indicators.note: heads points to the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: The bold young hero lopped off every one of the monster's heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Hercules cut off all the heads of the many-headed serpent of Lerna.
explanation.definitionFit: The many-headed water serpent was slain by Hercules as one of his labours.

clue.text: Tot has a play

parts.note: a tot is a small drink, a dram

explanation.surface: A small child takes part in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but it is a small shot of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage work is a play.

clue.text: Notice a dreadfully poisonous plant

indicators.note: dreadfully means the letters of notice a are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A warning sign about a dangerously toxic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood or wolfsbane, a toxic flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Cut off — one's going to ring after a delay

parts.note: one is I, plus 's for is, giving I and S
O is ring-shaped
late means arriving after a delay

explanation.surface: A caller is cut off while planning to phone back later.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to separate or cut off from others.

clue.text: Clean page going to press

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: A page is cleaned up before it goes to print.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse or rid of impurities, as with a purge of the system, is to clean.

clue.text: Get red card? Cheer up!

parts.note: to get something is to take it
a heart is a red playing card

explanation.surface: A footballer is sent off but told to stay cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red card' suggests football's sending-off; here it is a playing card of the red hearts suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to regain courage and become more hopeful.
